subject: Deployment selection & MAP — region constraints, POC waveplan, procurement gating

Subject: Deployment selection & MAP — region constraints, POC waveplan, procurement gating

Hi Claire / MedSync team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MedSync_MAP_v1.pdf) with milestones we discussed. High level proposal:

- Week 0: MAP kickoff and compliance intake (we'll complete SOC2 docs + security questionnaire)
- Week 1–2: POC (hosted) — run inference on a representative clinical workload, validate latency and token cost
- Week 3–4: Dedicated evaluation (if POC passes) — reserved pool sizing and SLA review
- Week 5: Decision gate and procurement / SOW signoff

To help us scope the POC properly, can you confirm the following by EOD Monday:
1) Production data residency requirement (country/region) — we heard "EU only" for prod but US for dev is ok?
2) Any mandatory network restrictions (private peering / IP allowlist / VPC-only)?
3) Procurement timeline and PO approver email.

If EU residency is required for production, recommended path is a staged approach: run the POC on hosted (EU region if available) with synthetic or redacted data, then run a short dedicated ramp to assess throughput under your SLA. Private (on‑prem or VPC) typically adds 4–6 weeks to timeline for packaging and network validation — we can include as an optional parallel track.

I've left rough estimates and decision points in the attached MAP. Next steps: I can circulate an updated MAP and a short host-vs-dedicated tradeoff doc once we get your residency confirmation.

Best,

Alex Martinez

Alex — thanks and appreciate the clear MAP. A few clarifications from our side:

- Production requirement: EU only (all PHI and patient identifiers must stay within EU for prod). POC can run in US if the data is tokenized/anonymized and you guarantee no persistent storage.
- Network: we will require private peering for dedicated and private models; hosted POC should be okay over TLS if data is anonymized.
- Procurement: our procurement cycle is ~3–4 weeks once we have a SOW and pricing. PO approver is Marie D'Souza (marie.dsouza@medsync.ai).

Attaching our security questionnaire with a few redlines — can you have your security team confirm?

Claire

Claire — thanks for the quick details, that's helpful. Short answers inline then a recommended path.

1) EU-only prod = understood. For POC we recommend two concrete paths:
   a) Hosted (EU region) POC: fastest to start (1 week onboarding). If we can host the POC in an EU region and use anonymized payloads, we can validate latency & cost quickly.
   b) Dedicated evaluation: reserved GPU pool in EU for throughput testing and SLA validation (adds ~2 weeks).
   c) Private (on-prem/VPC): full compliance, but adds 4–6 weeks for packaging, VPN/peering, and audit.

Tradeoffs:
- Latency: Private ~= Dedicated < Hosted (depending on region routing).
- Cost / unit economics: Hosted lowest up-front, Dedicated better at scale, Private highest OPEX/one-time.
- Time to closed: Hosted POC < Dedicated eval < Private deployment.

Recommended staged MAP:
- Phase 1 (Week 1): Hosted POC in EU region using redacted sample dataset (we can provide a data‑anonymization checklist).
- Phase 2 (Week 3): Dedicated 2-week evaluation if latency/throughput concerns remain.
- Phase 3 (Week 5–6): Procurement & SOW for production mode (Dedicated or Private depending on compliance signoff).

I updated the decision checkpoints in the MAP and will send MedSync_MAP_v2 after we confirm procurement contact and whether you want the POC in EU region or US anonymized. Also copying laura (CS) for onboarding cadence.

—Alex
